correctness.rationale: The central published lemma [2014 Lemma 8 and Theorem 2 proof] states exactly which Parikh vectors occur for each n: j runs through every integer p_n..q_n, and c=#0-#2 is 0 if n-j is even, and both ±1 if odd. Lemma 8 also proves the 4n-1 recurrences, yielding width k+1 at n_k=(2*4^k+1)/3. The weighted sum is ((a0+a2)n-(a0+a2-2a1)j+(a0-a2)c)/2. On a collision AΔj=EΔc with Δj≡Δc (mod 2) and |Δc|≤2. When A≠0 and A∤E, all cases force identical Parikh vectors. With A=0 at most three sums occur while at least k+2 vectors occur. With A≠0 and A|E, matching c=+1 at j against c=-1 at j-2E/A yields at least max(0,floor((k+2-2|E/A|)/2)) disjoint collision pairs. Thus deficits diverge. The public verifier passed on 14 finite sample lengths, 12 weight triples and 343 synthetic arithmetic triples; none of those computations are used as an infinite proof.
residual_risks: The theorem relies on correctness of the explicitly named published 2014 infinite Parikh-spectrum lemmas.
Finite factor computations cannot themselves establish the spectral completeness of the infinite word.

originality.rationale: The 2024 paper establishes preservation only along weights (0,1,lambda) for lambda>=5 and reports first losses for lambda=3,4. The present necessary-and-sufficient integer-triple divisibility phase diagram, plus divergence of deficits for every nonpreserving valuation, goes beyond that theorem. The 2014 paper already proves a strong complete Parikh-spectrum theorem: its data logically enable this deduction, but the weight classification and quantitative divergence are not asserted there and require new arithmetic and matching arguments. The 2025 study uses group-action quotient complexity rather than fixed sum maps, and the 2018 study concerns a different ternary morphism. A previously unindexed equivalent arithmetic corollary is possible.
residual_risks: An unindexed or implicit exposition could contain the same arithmetic consequence of the known 2014 complete Parikh spectrum.
Published 2014 structural characterization is the main mathematical input; no claim of originality of the Parikh-spectrum theorem.

value.rationale: The 2024 article explicitly motivates equality of additive and abelian complexities under valuation and proves only a sufficient one-parameter range. The result settles the whole integer-valuation problem for its concrete ternary square-free word, distinguishes exact arithmetic congruence phases (not just growth of weight separation), and proves every failed valuation loses unboundedly many classes at explicit lengths. In particular, increasing the largest weight from 7 to 8 in (0,2,*) flips the all-length preservation property, demonstrating information not available from an elementary magnitude bound. The infinite classification and divergence are mathematically natural, not arbitrary finite samples.
residual_risks: The proof is a short consequence of a previously known complete Parikh spectrum, so its significance is the new exact projection classification rather than an independent structural theory.
